topic: Military aviation - flares (decoys against heat-seeking missiles)
question: WHY SHOOT OUT
THESE FIREBALLS?
options: To light up the ground for photos
answer_full: To fool heat-seeking missiles. They're called decoy flares
recap: A military transport plane fires dozens of blinding fireballs out of its sides.
explain: Heat-seeking missiles steer towards the hottest thing they can see, usually the hot engines of the plane.
Each flare burns far hotter than the engine exhaust, so the missile's seeker locks onto the flare instead and flies away from the plane.
That's why crews sometimes fire them even before a launch is spotted. Modern missiles are harder to fool, so flares are only one layer of protection.
